candidates.rationale: Rising leverage compounds with elevated realized volatility into a distress-risk signal the market only reprices once a heavier debt load and higher price risk are jointly observed.

A firm whose leverage rank is climbing relative to peers while its profitability rank is simultaneously falling is deteriorating on both solvency and earnings quality at once, a joint-trajectory signal that absolute levels alone miss.
Profitability built on pricing power rather than sales volume marks a more defensible, less commoditized business, a quality distinction the market conflates when it looks only at blended ROA.

A firm flagged for aggressive income-increasing accruals has the least room to absorb the eventual earnings reversal when it is also highly levered, compounding accounting risk with balance-sheet fragility.

A worsening quarter-over-quarter accrual trend is a more urgent earnings-quality warning when the name is simultaneously drawing heavy trading attention, since that is when informed skepticism actually reaches the tape.
A genuine quarter-over-quarter margin improvement is more credible as a durable structural gain, rather than accounting noise, when it occurs in a name under unusually sustained trading scrutiny.

Leverage amplifies the real economic consequences of a large price move in either direction on any given day, since margin calls and covenant tests bind hardest exactly when the stock is already swinging.
Fast per-share book-value compounding deserves a valuation premium, but that story is credible, and less likely to reverse, only in names whose price has not been unusually turbulent.
A statistically cheap book-to-price ratio is a genuine bargain rather than a value trap only when the firm's earnings are also conservatively, not aggressively, accrued.

Firms whose profitability sits far from the cross-sectional average, whether exceptionally strong or exceptionally weak, are most likely mid re-rating exactly when that distinctiveness coincides with elevated trading attention.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.
